title: Routing Guardrails UX for Regional Tier Fallbacks and Model Variant Policies
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a purpose-driven user experience in the Console that prevents customers from creating routing policies that unintentionally increase latency, cost, or violate data residency constraints. This ticket scopes a set of guardrails, interactive validation, and a live preview/simulation panel for region selection, tier-based routing, and fallback model variants. The output should be a set of UX mockups and acceptance criteria the engineering team can implement alongside validation rules in the policy compiler.
goals: Allow customers to author region-aware rules with inline warnings when regulatory or cost thresholds are hit
Surface tier routing impacts (latency, estimated token-cost delta, capacity requirements) before saving
Provide deterministic fallback selection UI with compatibility checks (model signature, tokenizer, max sequence length)
Offer a live preview simulator that runs synthetic traffic scenarios and shows route decisions and percentage distribution
acceptance_criteria: Console policy editor surfaces guardrail warnings for data-residency mismatches and marks rules prevented from saving unless override is acknowledged
Preview simulator runs 3 traffic scenarios (low-latency, high-throughput, regulatory-constrained) and displays per-route metrics
Fallback variant selector validates model compatibility and shows implications (latency delta and quality risk estimate)
Policy save is blocked if a rule would exceed configured budget cap unless user explicitly enables a tolerant mode and signs a confirmation
Changes are persisted to policy manifests and reflected in runtime routing decisions in the Canary environment
dev_tasks: ENG-4829 - policy compiler: validation hooks for region & model constraints
ENG-5011 - console: preview simulator backend endpoints
ENG-5123 - console: UI components for guardrail banners and overrides
qa_criteria: Unit tests for compiler-level validation rules with edge cases (cross-region fallback, incompatible quantization)
E2E test that simulates 1000 synthetic requests in the preview and verifies route percentages match policy weights
Accessibility check for guardrail modal and keyboard flows
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Mateo), Design (Claire), and Security (Rohit). Agreed scope: editor warnings, preview simulator, and explicit override flow.
2026-02-20: Design draft v0.1 uploaded to Figma. Initial feedback: make cost delta more prominent and add a regulatory tag for geo-sensitive rules.
2026-02-28: Engineering spike completed. Compiler can evaluate 'region_residency' and return structured warnings. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2891
2026-03-05: PM review with Legal. Legal requested an explicit consent checkbox for policies that route to non-EU regions when account data residency is EU-locked.
2026-03-09: Design v0.3 addresses Legal feedback and introduces a two-step save when overrides are used. Figma link updated.
2026-03-12: Prototype demo to internal stakeholders. Observability team requested telemetry events for guardrail dismissals (event name: policy.guardrail.override). Adding to ENG-5123.
Next: finalize API contract for preview simulator and hand off to ENG-5011 implementation
comments: Claire (Design): We should show a small 'cost estimate' sparkline comparing the selected routing stack vs a conservative default.
Rohit (Security): Ensure any override is logged with user id and reason; consider requiring SSO group permissions for persistent overrides.
Mateo (Eng): Need to coordinate with runtime team for deterministic simulation logic; will schedule sync with Serving Runtime (ENG-4702).
risks: Incorrect compatibility checks could allow invalid fallback variants causing runtime errors
Overwhelming users with warnings may lead to habitual overrides and reduce the effectiveness of guardrails
Estimations for latency/cost are approximate; mismatches could erode trust if not clearly labeled as estimates
mitigations: Make compatibility checks conservative and fail-safe; mark uncertain checks as 'needs runtime validation'
Design progressive disclosure: show minimal warnings first and provide deep-dive guidance on request
Annotate all estimates with confidence bands and link to telemetry-powered post-save forecasts
implementation_notes: Preview simulator will accept a small synthetic workload spec (qps, seq_len_distribution, sample payload) and call a deterministic routing service endpoint
Guardrail rules implemented in compiler: region_residency, budget_cap, model_compatibility, legal_flag
UI needs an 'Override with acknowledgment' flow that creates an audit log entry and triggers a telemetry event
